newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan pharmaceutical group plans research firm.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan pharmaceutical group plans research firm.

text.p: The Taiwan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association said on Tuesday it would seek T$3.5 billion (US$127 million) in private and government investment to form a pharmaceutical research company.
The association said it had an initial commitment from Vice Premier Hsu Li-teh to have the cabinet's Development Fund finance 40 percent or T$1.4 billion of the venture.

"Aside from the 40 percent government fund, we hope to gather another 30 percent from private pharmaceutical firms and the remaining 30 percent from major investment firms," the association's executive director Liu Chin-chien said by telephone.

Liu said about 10 local pharmaceutical firms had agreed to join the project, including China Chemical and Pharmaceutical, Yung Shin Pharmaceutical Industry, Standard Chemical and Pharmaceutical and Sintong Chemical Industrial.
The joint venture firm would specialise in research and development of pharmaceutical products, but would not engage in production or sales.
"The firm will gather the newest pharmaceutical technologies and products from abroad, perform further research on them and make them suitable for the local Taiwan market," Liu said.
"The company seeks to make up for Taiwan's lack of upstream pharmaceutical research to coordinate with mid- and downstream production and delivery," he added.
Liu said the company would begin operation whenever the Cabinet's Development Fund and private companies finalise their investment plans, but was unable to predict when that might be.
